name: framework-choice-by-needs
description: GoogleTest and Catch2 are chosen by project properties rather than presented as equal options
prompt: Choose and pin one test framework for a new C++17 network service. We need typed tests, value-parameterized tests, and mocks for one OS socket boundary. The organization already uses CTest but has no C++ framework standard.
trap: The model says both GoogleTest and Catch2 are fine and leaves the decision to taste, or picks Catch2 and then adds a second mocking framework without accounting for the extra stack.
criteria: Chooses GoogleTest because the requirements include typed tests, parameterization, and integrated GoogleMock
Pins a release compatible with C++17 rather than tracking a branch
Registers the executable through gtest_discover_tests and CTest
Keeps mocking limited to the OS socket boundary

name: ctest-is-entry-point
description: Tests are discoverable and selectable through the shared CTest graph
prompt: Our GoogleTest binary runs locally as ./parser_tests, but ctest --preset dev reports 'No tests were found'. Add the missing CMake registration and show how CI runs only Parser tests with failure output.
trap: The model tells CI to invoke the binary directly, creating a second test entry point and leaving CTest unaware of individual cases.
criteria: Links the test binary with GTest::gtest_main or an explicit main
Runs the subset through ctest --preset dev -R Parser

name: fake-before-internal-mocks
description: A test uses a real value or fake instead of mocking every collaborator
prompt: A Repository test currently mocks Clock, Record, Serializer, VectorStorage, and Logger and asserts 18 calls in order. Only the remote object store is slow and failure-prone. Refactor the testing approach without changing production behavior.
trap: The model updates the mock expectations to match the implementation, preserving a brittle interaction test that fails on harmless refactors.
criteria: Keeps a mock or controlled fake only at the remote object-store boundary
Uses real value objects and serializer behavior where cheap
Asserts repository outcomes rather than incidental call order
Does not expose private members solely for the test

name: separate-sanitizer-builds
description: ASan+UBSan and TSan run in separate configurations
prompt: Add sanitizer coverage to a GCC/Clang C++17 test matrix. A teammate proposed one preset with -fsanitize=address,undefined,thread and a retry for race failures. Correct the design and explain how to read failures.
trap: The model combines incompatible ASan and TSan runtimes and masks races with retries instead of creating deterministic synchronization.
criteria: Creates one ASan+UBSan build and a separate TSan build
Applies sanitizer flags at both compile and link time
Keeps a normal unsanitized test run
Starts diagnosis from the first report and adds a focused regression test
Does not use retry as the fix for a project-owned race
